title: Beauty Salon Interior Design 63 m² | DUMSKAYA DESIGN
description: 63 m² beauty salon: interior design and technical drawings. DUMSKAYA DESIGN, Bratislava and Vienna.

parts.html: An interior design project for a 63 m² beauty salon, with technical documentation for the renovation. Within this area we fit a reception desk with a waiting area, workstations for hairdressers, manicurists and a brow artist, a cosmetologist’s room, a restroom and a back room for staff. The zones follow the way the salon works: from the entrance the client comes to the desk and the waiting area, then to the stylists’ chairs, with the service rooms at the back.

By the entrance stands a white reception desk with rounded corners. Behind it is a light wood shelving unit with vertical dividers for retail cosmetics, and three pebble-shaped pendant lights hang above the desk. The waiting area is by the large window: soft bouclé armchairs and a side table on a solid pedestal base.

The hairdressing stations are separated by plastered partitions with rounded ends. Each has a built-in arched mirror with perimeter lighting and a floating light wood console. The chairs are beige on chrome bases. The wall behind the manicure tables carries sculpted faces in relief against vertical slats, reflected in the mirrors of the hairdressing stations.

The manicure tables, with rounded tops, drawers and built-in dust extraction, are placed by the window, each with a ring light and a rolling stool for the manicurist. The brow artist’s station is screened off. The cosmetologist has a separate treatment room.

The back room is set up as a kitchenette: light floor-to-ceiling cabinets, open niches, and a table for quick meals with a fridge under the countertop. At the sink there is a backsplash of textured terracotta tiles and a black faucet.

The whole palette is built on shades of white and beige: large-format light porcelain tiles on the floor, matte plaster on the walls and light wood furniture. General lighting comes from recessed spotlights, with lit mirrors at the workstations. Ventilation and air conditioning are part of the design: the grilles and ducts are visible in the visualizations. More of our work for businesses is in the commercial interior design section.
